content:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Datadog ingestion delay detected (us-east-1, eu-west-1). Logs/metrics ingestion latency spiking >5m. Source: dd-integ-alert. Please triage.
Priya: I'm oncall. Acknowledging and standing up timeline.
Luca: pulling dd status and our scrapers — status.datadoghq.com shows degraded ingestion, "queue backlog" on logs pipeline.
Nina: seeing silence on some dashboards; alert totals drop to zero around 11:32 UTC. That looks like missing ingest rather than our agents.
Raj: support: two customers reporting missing alerts. One is on Dedicated cluster (cust-rodin). I'll flag their account as high priority and notify success.
Priya: mitigation options: 1) enable alternate metrics sink (prometheus pushgateway) for critical alerting 2) increase local agent disk buffer and retention 3) route critical PagerDuty notifications via webhook fallback.
Luca: I can flip the pushgateway. Patch command: ```bash
kubectl -n ops patch configmap observability-sink -p '{"data":{"sink":"pushgateway","priority":"critical-only"}}'
```
SRE-Bot: Automation run: applied patch to ops namespace by Luca at 1772100055. Pushgateway routing enabled for priority=critical.
Nina: enabling additional buffering on agents: ```bash
for node in $(cat nodes.txt); do ssh $node "sudo systemctl set-environment VECTOR_FILE_BUFFER_BYTES=20000000 && sudo systemctl restart vector"; done
```
Raj: done on canaries (3 nodes) — agents report increased local buffer and write-ahead files.
Priya: switching PagerDuty webhook fallback now so critical alerts don't rely on Datadog alert forwarding. Command: ```bash
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS' https://internal-api.redwood.io/fallbacks/pd -d '{"enable":true,"scope":"critical"}'
```
Luca: executed, webhook fallback active. Sending test alert to PD: test alert sent and acknowledged.
Priya: good. Customer comms: draft status note - "We detected Datadog ingestion delays causing delayed alerts and partial dashboard gaps. We've enabled fallbacks and increased buffering. We will continue to monitor and will update in 30 minutes." Approve?
Raj: approve. I'll send to impacted customers and mark as incident update on our status page.
Incident Bot: Status updated on Datadog: root cause listed as upstream ingest queue overflow, recovery ETA ~60-90 minutes. Link: https://status.datadoghq.com/incidents/ef56
Nina: impact assessment: metrics latency increased; some non-critical dashboards showing sparse data. Core inference services continue to operate normally. Risk: short-term blindspot for logs/ingest and delayed alert triggers.
Priya: created PD incident PD-RED-6789 and notified leadership slack #exec-alerts. Handoff plan: I'm primary until 12:30 UTC, then Luca will take over.
Luca: I'll take over at 12:30. Leave me any runbook steps.
Priya: runbook steps added to PD case: applied pushgateway, increased buffer on agents, enabled PD webhook fallback, canary checks passed.
Raj: adding mitigation — enable local file-forwarding to S3 as long-term capture to avoid data loss: ```bash
kubectl apply -f s3-forwarder.yaml -n observability
```
Nina: applying to canary first. If successful, roll to 100% so logs will be stored in S3 even if DD backlog persists.
Luca: canary completed, S3 forwarder succeeded, starting gradual rollout.
Incident Bot: SRE telemetry: pushgateway routing active, buffer size +20MB on 12 nodes, s3-forwarder canary OK. Will post another update on Datadog recovery.
Priya: customer impact summary for comms: delayed alerts (30-90m), missing short-term logs for some services, no inference correctness impact, no PII exposure observed.
Raj: filed support tickets for affected accounts and set follow-ups.
Luca: prepping rollback notes in case Datadog recovers: commands to disable pushgateway and s3-forwarder and reduce buffer.
Priya: handing off now to Luca at 12:30 UTC. Luca has PD and all links.
Luca: taking over. Monitoring Datadog and our fallbacks. If anything new comes up, post here.
Incident Bot: NOTE: ongoing thread. Please paste any customer replies or new infra anomalies here for timeline.
Nina: proposed postmortem owner: Raj. He'll collect timeline and recommend automations to toggle fallbacks automatically based on Datadog health signals.
Raj: accepted. I'll start draft and include steps to automate fallback with a cool-down and alerting to ops.
Luca: FYI — Datadog status reports partial recovery at 12:55 UTC, ingestion backlog decreasing. Watching for backfill and alert reconciliation.
Priya: thanks team. We'll keep monitoring until metrics fully reconcile.
